outcome: indications for surgery (suspicion of malignancy, large growth, ovarian cyst torsion)
cohort: The study included 30 pregnant women with pathologically confirmed ovarian endometrioma, 21 of whom underwent laparoscopic surgery during pregnancy and 9 underwent cystectomy during cesarean section.
finding: Ovarian endometrioma (OMA) exhibits varied changes during pregnancy, frequently necessitating surgical intervention due to suspected malignancy which is challenging to differentiate from decidualization, with laparoscopic surgery appearing safe in mid-pregnancy and recurrence being a concern postpartum.
mod_finding: Nine patients underwent cystectomy during cesarean section, with some experiencing decidualization in postoperative pathology and one case of recurrence during follow-up.
